name: Tiene
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Ellington, John Ernest. 1977. Aspects of the Tiene language. PhD dissertation, University of Wisconsin (229pp grammar, Glottolog's most extensive description)

new_statements.quote: Le kɪtíínɪ́ atteste deux tons de base: haut et bas représentés respectivement ici par l'accent aigu et généralement par l'absence de tout signe diacritique pour des raisons d'économie. La contraction vocalique (3.1.) permet de la génération des tons complexes (montant et descendant). Quelques racines ont été cependant notées facultativement avec un ton descendant. [...] Les tons ont une valeur à la fois lexicale et grammaticale.
new_statements.translation: Kitiini has two basic tones: high and low, represented here respectively by the acute accent and, in general, by the absence of any diacritic, for reasons of economy. Vowel contraction (3.1.) allows the generation of complex tones (rising and falling). Some roots have, however, optionally been noted with a falling tone. [...] Tones have both lexical and grammatical value.
new_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2004. Esquisse du ketiene, petite unité du bantou B.80. Journal of Asian and African Studies 67: 105-150.
new_statements.locator: §2.4.1 'Tons', p. 120 (scanned page 16), and 'Valeur des tons', p. 122 (scanned page 18)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (46-page image-only scan, TUFS repository) and rendered PDF pages 16 and 18 (printed pp. 120 and 122) to PNG; both quoted passages are on the page images exactly as reported: p. 120 §2.4.1 'Tons': "Le kɪtíínɪ́ atteste deux tons de base: haut et bas représentés respectivement ici par l'accent aigu et généralement par l'absence de tout signe diacritique pour des raisons d'économie. La contraction vocalique (3.1.) permet de la génération des tons complexes (montant et descendant). Quelques racines ont été cependant notées facultativement avec un ton descendant." and p. 122 'Valeur des tons': "Les tons ont une valeur à la fois lexicale et grammaticale." (the report's "[...]" correctly ma…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tiene is described as a two-tone language (H vs L, contour tones from vowel contraction, tone lexically and grammatically contrastive, with sentence-level metatony, downstep and pausal lowering). The sketch says nothing at all about word stress, intensity or prominence; no stress position can be read from it. Vowel length is phonemic (p. 110) and not tied to any position.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress (none discussed). Tonal remarks: *LH, *HH, *HL patterns generally became LL in citation; infinitive final -a is realised H phrase-medially (metatony); optative stems are uniformly L.
new_statements.domain_note: The tone remarks distinguish citation forms ('en citation') from phrase-medial and phrase-final realisations; nothing about a stress domain. Closed syllables arise only at phrase level by final-vowel elision (p. 123).
new_statements.identity_note: Motingea Mangulu 2004 describes 'ketiene/kitiini' (Tiene, Guthrie B.81 = tien1242) from data of three Tiene students at ISP Mbandaka (1993), principal informant from the Nkete (southern) dialect group, checked in 2004 with speakers of the central Dya group in Kinshasa (p. 108 §1.4); Ellington 1977 distinguishes five dialect groups (Mfuome, Nkete, Ngee-ntaana, Dya, Inkonya; p. 107). Motingea treats Tiene as a variety close to Boma (B.82) rather than to the rest of Tio-Teke; still the same languoid tien1242.

sources.note: Section 2 'Phonétique et phonologie' (pp. 109-125) has 2.1 vowels (7 vowels, phonemic length, p. 110), 2.2 consonants, 2.3 semi-vowels, 2.4 'Tons et syllabes' (pp. 120-123): two basic tones H and L, contour tones from vowel contraction, metatony/downstep/pausal low, tones both lexical and grammatical (p. 122); syllable types CV, CSV, V, N (p. 123). Nothing on stress, intensity or prominence anywhere in the 46 pages (grep of scanned for accent/intensité/proéminence/prosodie: only 'accent aigu' as the H-tone diacritic).

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2006. Affixation by place of articulation: Rare AND mysterious. UC Berkeley PhonLab Annual Report 2: 145-184. DOI 10.5070/P70dd909zp (pre-print of Hyman 2010, in Wohlgemuth & Cysouw (eds.), Rara & Rarissima, De Gruyter Mouton, 145-184).
sources.note: Morphology paper (verb extensions realised as infixes); all Tiene data from Ellington 1977. Section 3 'The prosodic stem in Tiene' concerns stem shape (three-syllable maximum, place-of-articulation restrictions) and vowel lengthening; no mention of stress or accent; tone mentioned only in passing ('with tone change').
